content: Use induction on n. For n>=2 perform descending column operations C_k <- C_k - x_1 C_{k-1} for k=n,...,2, so C_{k-1} is still original. The transformed first row is (1,0,...,0); each remaining row contributes x_i-x_1. Expansion at (1,1) leaves the Vandermonde matrix on x_2,...,x_n, to which induction applies. This proof never divides, so repeated x_i cause no issue.
